title: [ML] fixes bug with composite agg datafeed extraction

timeline.message: [ML] fixes bug with composite agg datafeed extraction
timeline.author: Benjamin Trent

timeline.body:
If a `max` value in a given composite aggregation bucket is the same as the current after page floor, the datafeed could cancel processing composite aggregation pages too early.

It will see that `max` timestamp aligned with the interval and stop processing. This is a bug. There may be still other terms
to process within that `date_histogram` bucket in subsequent pages as the order of the buckets are done by term NOT by max timestamp.

This commit corrects this to verify that if the process is canceled, the datafeed continues to finish out the current date_histogram bucket, regardless if the first timestamp seen after cancelling aligns with the current page or not.

closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/71212
if `afterKeyTimeBucket` is the floor, then could this not be simplified to always be `nextBucketOnCancel = afterKeyTimeBucket + interval` ?

reply.body:
This ALMOST works. 

Our considerations are:
- 1. We iterate a given page in order of the `max` timestamp
- 2. A `max` timestamp for a bucket will always be within that bucket and interval `max -> [bucket, bucket+interval)`
- 3. A page could have multiple `date_histogram` buckets
- 4. Two pages could have out of order `max` timestamps as the paging order is predicated on bucket floor + terms
- 5. A cancel could occur at any time

If we take considerations 4 and 5, the timestamp at the moment of cancellation could be within a subsequent bucket. This may be 1 or more date_histogram buckets above the current page. 

Lets ponder:
 - our interval is `1000` 
 - we are on page `1000`
 - The current page passed over into the next bucket with a timestamp `2500`
 - Cancel is handled
 - If we simply set the `nextBucketOnCancel = afterKeyTimeBucket + interval`, the cancellation would be `2000`
 - We erroneously end before finishing the current `date_histogram` bucket (which is now `2000`)

Having monotonically iterating `max` timestamps within a given page is nice as it allows us to know when we have cross over into the next page and ONCE we have cross over into the next page, we know that all `max` timestamps will be AT LEAST as big as the floor of the next bucket. So, we can say with certainty once cross the floor of the next bucket, we are done.
Got it. But I think we can get away with `Intervals.alignToFloor(timestamp + interval, interval)`
100%, I think this works. Will update. Fewer if statements == fewer bugs (usually).
